newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan army renews thrust against rebel camps.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan army renews thrust against rebel camps.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops on Monday launched a new offensive against Tamil Tiger guerrilla jungle bases in the Indian Ocean island's east, a military spokesman said.
"It's a limited operation to flush out terrorists from their jungle camps," he said. "No fighting has been reported so far."

The army's elite air mobile and special forces brigades were advancing from several directions against rebel bases in the jungles of Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) east of the capital Colombo, military officials said.
Troops were backed by aircraft and artillery while the navy patrolled offshore to prevent rebels escaping by sea and to provide fire support and evacuate casualties if required, they said.
The commandos were operating in small groups, laying ambushes for Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels trying to flee, they said.
The rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the island, usually withdraw in the face of the advancing army and avoid battle, officials said.
Government troops hunting the Tigers in the Batticaloa jungles last week destroyed two abandoned rebel bases.
The Tigers were not immediately available for comment on the military's reports of the latest action.
The Tigers said last week that they had lost more than 9,000 members in their war for independence, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The rebels say the toll is much higher.
